section_summary: This section follows claims for the restitution of the Hirondelle, Islas Visayas and Eldorado, alongside United States policy work on Japanese merchant shipping reparations. Later documents debate the size and operation of Japan’s postwar fleet, shipbuilding capacity, and the use of Japanese-controlled vessels in foreign trade. The section ends with a Chinese report on Japanese shipping, fishing and possible ship orders.

subfiles.title: Restitution of Islas Visayas: concluding note
subfiles.about: The Department offers to transmit papers to Tokyo for Panama’s vessel claim.
subfiles.summary: British owners and the Panamanian government are to be informed about steps needed to conclude the claim.

subfiles.title: Restitution of S.S. Hirondelle
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The adviser reports that the Hirondelle is available for restitution and asks which government should claim it.
subfiles.summary: Shipping registers indicate a change from American to Philippine ownership and registry before the war. The Civil Property Custodian requests proof of title and acquisition circumstances, plus the owners’ wishes on repair and refitting.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning S.S. Hirondelle
subfiles.about: The Department directs that the Hirondelle ordinarily be treated as a Philippine vessel.
subfiles.summary: Maritime Commission records show its transfer to Vicente Madrigal before Japanese seizure in Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on Japanese merchant shipping claims
subfiles.about: Hilldring submits the State Department’s proposed reparations position for circulation.
subfiles.summary: Requests committee consideration of the attached policy paper.

subfiles.title: Statement of U.S. Position with Respect to Reparations Claims to Japanese Merchant Shipping
subfiles.about: The paper proposes allocating Japanese merchant vessels according to proven wartime shipping losses against Japan.
subfiles.summary: It recommends claims only for losses during each claimant’s belligerency against Japan, with any remainder distributed by general industrial reparations shares. Its appendices cite occupation directives and argue against Britain’s proposal to count worldwide shipping losses, which could broaden other reparations claims.

subfiles.title: Panamanian note concerning Islas Visayas, English translation
subfiles.about: Panama acknowledges information about the vessel and forwards it to its foreign minister.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador thanks the Secretary for information about the ship at Hakodate.

subfiles.title: Panamanian note concerning Islas Visayas, Spanish original
subfiles.about: The original Spanish note acknowledges information about Islas Visayas.
subfiles.summary: States that the earlier note was forwarded to Panama’s foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Telegram urging restrictions on German and Japanese ships
subfiles.about: McIlvaine urges treaty limits on German and Japanese ocean-going ships.
subfiles.summary: He proposes confiscation of prohibited ships and cites his Panama Canal service.

subfiles.title: White House referral of McIlvaine telegram
subfiles.about: The White House refers McIlvaine’s telegram for consideration.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the telegram to the Department.

subfiles.title: Reply to C. A. McIlvaine
subfiles.about: Martin acknowledges McIlvaine’s proposed restrictions on German and Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: Says the Department is considering restrictions to protect the United States.

subfiles.title: Research studies for the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Stelle responds to a request for studies, including one on Japan’s merchant marine.
subfiles.summary: He lists reports being supplied and suggests a newer textile study in place of an outdated one.

subfiles.title: Claim for restitution of S.S. Islas Visayas
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Civil Property Custodian asks whether Panama intends to file a formal claim.
subfiles.summary: No Panamanian claim has yet reached occupation authorities.

subfiles.title: Reply on Islas Visayas claim
subfiles.about: The Department explains delays in obtaining a Panamanian claim for Islas Visayas.
subfiles.summary: Panamanian and British embassies have been reminded; coordination with the Hong Kong owners will take time.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendment to SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.about: Martin proposes extending reparations disposal rules to merchant shipping.
subfiles.summary: The amendment would let the United States dispose of shipping received beyond its own needs.

subfiles.title: Draft amendment to SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.about: A draft requests committee approval to include merchant ships in the reparations disposal clause.
subfiles.summary: It applies the industrial equipment transfer rule to merchant vessels.

subfiles.title: Formal request for amendment to SWNCC 236/35
subfiles.about: Hilldring formally submits the amendment covering Japanese merchant shipping.
subfiles.summary: The proposed wording restricts resale or barter for three years while preserving United States discretion to allocate surplus claims politically.

subfiles.title: Forwarding approved SWNCC 236/42
subfiles.about: The committee forwards its approved merchant shipping reparations paper.
subfiles.summary: Sends SWNCC 236/42 for implementation.

subfiles.title: Decision on SWNCC 236/42
subfiles.about: The secretaries record approval of SWNCC 236/42 on June 24.
subfiles.summary: Records the committee’s approval.

subfiles.title: Note circulating SWNCC 236/42
subfiles.about: The Secretariat circulates the subcommittee’s merchant shipping report.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Joint Chiefs of Staff were asked for military comments.

subfiles.title: Statement of U.S. Position with Respect to Reparations Claims to Japanese Merchant Shipping, SWNCC 236/42
subfiles.from: SWNCC Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: The report sets out a proposed basis for claims against Japanese merchant ships.
subfiles.summary: It postpones fixing available tonnage, then proposes distributing eligible ships according to proven losses during war against Japan. Claimants would be invited after tonnage is determined. Appendices review Allied directives and explain why worldwide shipping losses should not govern Japanese reparations.

subfiles.title: Submission of merchant shipping position to Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.from: Philander P. Claxton Jr., for J. H. Hilldring
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: The approved United States position is sent for presentation to the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Requests a Far Eastern Commission policy decision.

subfiles.title: Conclusions on Japanese merchant shipping reparations
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: The enclosure states the United States conclusions on shipping reparations.
subfiles.summary: Sets eligibility, allocation and consultation rules for claims.

subfiles.title: Eldorado restitution claim
subfiles.about: The adviser reports that the Panamanian-registered Eldorado is salvageable in Hakata Bay.
subfiles.summary: Requests that Panama be invited to submit ownership and seizure evidence for restitution.

subfiles.title: Instructions to embassy on Eldorado
subfiles.about: The embassy is asked to invite a formal Panamanian claim for Eldorado.
subfiles.summary: Requests the evidence specified in Tokyo’s airgram.

subfiles.title: Diplomatic note on Eldorado
subfiles.about: The Department informs Panama that Eldorado is salvageable and describes the claims process.
subfiles.summary: A formal claim should include a vessel description, proof of ownership and an account of Japanese acquisition.

subfiles.title: Reply to Professor Sheldon
subfiles.about: Lydman sends a Japanese merchant marine report and offers to discuss Sheldon’s project.
subfiles.summary: Expresses interest in the Far Eastern Institute’s work.

subfiles.title: Letter presenting observations on Japan’s merchant marine
subfiles.about: Nakashima submits an attached study advocating restoration of Japanese merchant shipping.
subfiles.summary: He argues that war losses and foreign freight costs impede Japan’s economic recovery. He welcomes a recommendation for ship construction and asks Kennan to consider the attached case for a larger fleet.

subfiles.title: Some Observations on the Future of the Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: Nakashima argues for a larger Japanese fleet and a staged return of ship operation to private owners.
subfiles.summary: Using prewar freight and trade figures, he contends that a shipping ceiling near 2.5 million tons would damage Japan’s balance of payments; he estimates a need of about 4.49 million tons. He rejects the claim that merchant shipping alone poses a military danger. He also criticizes government vessel management and mixed crews, proposing time charters that restore maintenance, manning and operation to owners while retaining state direction of cargoes.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file comments on maritime dispute
subfiles.about: A reader comments on a dispute involving the War Department, the Maritime Commission and TRC.
subfiles.summary: Suggests an informal discussion with Morse; parts are illegible.

subfiles.title: Use of SCAJAP Shipping for Japanese Foreign Trade and Relief Shipments
subfiles.about: Johnson forwards conflicting views on priority use of SCAJAP ships for trade and relief cargo.
subfiles.summary: He explains that Army efforts to save dollars by using Japanese-controlled vessels could displace American commercial carriers. Three communications are enclosed for the Department’s information.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission letter on SCAJAP priorities
subfiles.about: Norris warns that proposed SCAJAP cargo priorities threaten American shipping interests.
subfiles.summary: He lists the proposed carrier order and challenges using rate reductions to support Japan’s trade balance. He asks the Commission to scrutinize Army plans and establish operating rules.

subfiles.title: Army radio on shipping arrangements for relief cargo
subfiles.about: The Army clarifies responsibility for obtaining vessels and gives suitable SCAJAP ships first priority.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes central charter procurement from limited theater discretion over small urgent shipments.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission radio challenging SCAJAP commercial carriage
subfiles.about: The regional office objects to using loaned Commission ships to free Japanese vessels for commercial voyages.
subfiles.summary: It seeks either the return of loaned tonnage or an Army agreement to leave commercial cargo, including relief shipments, to commercial carriers.

subfiles.title: Status of Eldorado claim
subfiles.about: The Department reports Panama’s intention to pursue restitution of Eldorado.
subfiles.summary: Says Panama’s legation in China is being instructed to file a claim.

subfiles.title: Consultation with Maritime Commission on Japanese fleet policy
subfiles.about: Radius recommends seeking Maritime Commission views on proposed Japanese fleet and shipbuilding changes.
subfiles.summary: He says the War Department should consult the Commission because it sponsors the proposed changes.

subfiles.title: Japanese Shipbuilding and Merchant Shipping
subfiles.about: Whitman recommends more Japanese shipbuilding capacity and no removals from the current fleet as reparations.
subfiles.summary: He proposes 300,000 gross tons of annual capacity and argues that Japan needs its existing vessels for recovery.

subfiles.title: Forwarding study regarding Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: Sebald summarizes and forwards a Japanese Foreign Ministry brochure on shipping needs.
subfiles.summary: The brochure argues that freight earnings once offset Japan’s trade deficit and that foreign ships alone cannot carry future imports economically. It estimates a need for about four million gross tons and adequate shipyards. Sebald says the mission will later submit its own assessment.

subfiles.title: Remarks of China Merchants Steam Navigation Company general manager
subfiles.about: The consulate forwards a translated report of Oliver Zi’s remarks after visiting Japan.
subfiles.summary: It highlights reported shipbuilding gains and obstacles facing Chinese traders.

subfiles.title: Ta Kung Pao report on Japanese shipping
subfiles.about: The report recounts Oliver Zi’s views on Japanese shipping, fishing, reparations and Chinese ship orders.
subfiles.summary: Zi discusses Japan’s fleet and shipyards, Chinese demands for reparations ships, proposed passenger vessels in exchange for Hainan ore, and barriers to Sino-Japanese trade.
